w: Built on the patch of the former Harland & Wolff yard where the Titanic herself took shape, this steel-clad visitor centre opened in 2012 as Belfast's monument to its own maritime past. Over 12,000 square metres of galleries trace the ship's construction and 1912 sinking, alongside sister liners Olympic and Britannic.
s: Built on the very slipway where the Titanic was born
_facts: Visitor attraction opened in 2012 on the site of the former Harland & Wolff shipyard in Titanic Quarter
A monument to Belfast's maritime heritage where the RMS Titanic was built
Tells the stories of the Titanic and her sister ships RMS Olympic and HMHS Britannic
More than 12,000 square metres of floor space, mostly galleries and function rooms
